name: Bronze Age
description: The age of the first cities, states, and writing systems, defined by bronze metallurgy and long-distance tin trade. Sumer, Egypt, the Indus cities, Shang China, Minoan Crete, and the Hittites flourished within interlocking exchange networks.

name: Iron Age
description: Cheaper, harder iron democratized tools and weapons after the Bronze Age Collapse. Alphabets spread with Phoenician trade, Israel and Greece took shape, and Assyria built the first true universal empire.

name: Classical Antiquity
description: The Greco-Roman world from Homer to the fall of the western empire: the polis and citizenship, philosophy and drama, Roman law and engineering — the canon later ages repeatedly 'renaissanced'.

name: Islamic Golden Age
description: Under the Abbasid caliphate, Baghdad's House of Wisdom translated and extended Greek, Persian, and Indian learning — algebra, optics, medicine, astronomy — while trade knit Afro-Eurasia from Córdoba to Samarkand. Conventionally closed by the Mongol sack of Baghdad.

name: High Middle Ages
description: Europe's medieval apogee: population doubling, Gothic cathedrals, the first universities, scholasticism, chartered towns, and the Crusades — before climate downturn and plague reversed the boom.

name: The Renaissance
description: The rebirth of classical learning and naturalistic art radiating from the Italian city-states: humanism, perspective, printing, and the patronage economics of Medici Florence — shading into the Scientific Revolution and the age of exploration.

name: Age of Exploration
description: Iberian navigators, driven by spices, gold, and faith and enabled by the caravel and new cartography, linked the world's oceans — da Gama to India, Columbus to the Americas, Magellan's fleet around the globe — beginning European maritime empire.

name: The Enlightenment
description: The 'age of reason': confidence that rational inquiry could reform knowledge, religion, and government. Locke, Voltaire, Rousseau, Kant, the Encyclopédie, and salon culture furnished the ideas of the American and French revolutions.

name: Industrial Revolution
description: Steam power, factory production, railways, and telegraphy — beginning in British textiles — multiplied output and urban populations, remade class structures, and opened the great divergence between industrialized and colonized economies.

name: The Cold War
description: Four decades of global rivalry between the American and Soviet blocs, waged through nuclear deterrence, proxy wars, espionage, and the space race rather than direct great-power war — ending with the Soviet collapse.

name: Information Age
description: The era defined by the microprocessor, personal computer, internet, and mobile phone: economies reorganized around data and software, and most of humanity connected to a single communications fabric within two generations.
